:::{#exr-wilks-std-gaussian}
#### Standardizing an approximately Gaussian estimate

Suppose $\hthml \dsim \ndist{\th_0, \einf(\th_0)^{-1}}$,
and define $Z \eqdef \sqrt{\einf(\th_0)}\,(\hthml - \th_0)$.
Show that $Z$ is approximately standard Gaussian,
and find the approximate distribution of $Z^2$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-wilks-std-gaussian}

$Z$ is a linear function of $\hthml$,
so it is approximately Gaussian,
with approximate mean and variance:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{Z}
&= \sqrt{\einf(\th_0)}\,\paren{\E{\hthml} - \th_0}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&\approx \sqrt{\einf(\th_0)}\,(\th_0 - \th_0)
&& \text{(approximate mean of $\hthml$)}\\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Var{Z}
&= \einf(\th_0) \Var{\hthml}
&& \text{($\Var{aY + b} = a^2 \Var{Y}$)}\\
&\approx \einf(\th_0) \einf(\th_0)^{-1}
&& \text{(approximate variance of $\hthml$)}\\
&= 1
\end{aligned}
$$

So $Z \dsim \ndist{0, 1}$.
The square of a standard Gaussian variable has a $\chi^2_1$ distribution,
so $Z^2$ has approximately a $\chi^2_1$ distribution.

:::
